transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. What brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Um... well, I guess I'm here because of elevators. It's really stupid because I know they aren't actually dangerous or anything. But whenever I have to get in one, I just get so scared, like I'm gonna get trapped in there, and I just can't make myself feel normal about it. 

It's becoming a bit of an issue at work. I do construction, mostly framing, and usually it's fine because we do a lot of low-rise stuff. Though my buddy Mike—he fell off a ladder on a job last year and snapped his collarbone. He was out for like three months, and when he finally came back, the foreman made him sit in the tool trailer all day doing inventory. He was so mad. That trailer smells awful, like old coffee and wet sawdust, you know? Plus the radio in there only picks up this one fuzzy country station. 

But anyway, yeah... if I have to ride up in a closed-in elevator, my brain just totally panics about being stuck in that box.
Do you feel this kind of fear only in elevators, or does it happen in other situations too, like crowded places, driving, or being in small or enclosed spaces?

Um, no, I don't think so. It's pretty much just elevators. Like, driving is totally fine. I actually really like driving. I drive the crew truck for work sometimes, this huge beat-up diesel Ford. 

My boss makes me keep all the fuel receipts in this little plastic folder tucked into the sun visor. But last week, it was so hot out that the plastic literally melted to the windshield. Just completely fused to the glass. We had to use a putty knife and some of that Goof Off spray to scrape it away. It took almost an hour, and the whole cab smelled like harsh chemicals for days. My dog hated it. I have a pitbull mix, Buster, and he usually loves riding shotgun, you know, hanging his head out the window to catch the breeze. But he wouldn't even get in the truck until I rode around with the windows down for a while to air it out. He's really picky about smells. 

So, um... wait, what were you asking? Oh, right, driving and stuff. Yeah, no, driving doesn't scare me at all. Just the elevator thing.
Have you ever experienced sudden feelings of intense fear or discomfort, like your heart racing, sweating, or feeling like you can't breathe — even when you're not in an elevator?

Um, no... I don't think I get those out of nowhere. Like, my heart will race if I'm running late or something, but not just sitting around. I mean, unless I drink too much coffee. I used to drink those huge energy drinks, the ones with the neon green tabs? But they made my hands shake so bad I couldn't even hold a hammer straight. 

My sister drinks them like water. She works at this warehouse, pulling orders all night, and she says she needs them to stay awake. But I swear, she's gonna give herself a heart attack. She already has high blood pressure, and she refuses to eat anything green. Last Thanksgiving, I tried to get her to try some of my green bean casserole—the kind with the crispy onions on top, you know? It's my grandma's recipe. But she literally picked around the beans and just ate the onions. It drove my mom crazy. Mom spent like three days cooking and cleaning the house. She even bought these fancy new curtains for the dining room, but they were too long and kept dragging on the floor, so the cat kept attacking them. 

But yeah, no, I don't get panicky like that unless I'm looking at an elevator.
When you think about getting into an elevator, is your main fear being trapped inside, or is it something else that worries you more?

Um, yeah, I guess being trapped is the main thing. Just the thought of the doors closing and then... what if it gets stuck between floors, you know? It's just a metal box. 

Speaking of metal boxes, my cousin bought this old shipping container last month to use as a shed in his backyard. He got it cheap from some auction down by the port. But getting it delivered was a total nightmare. The truck driver backed over his neighbor's mailbox—like, completely flattened it into the dirt. It was one of those fancy brick ones, too, not just a wooden post. The neighbor was furious, obviously, and came out yelling in his bathrobe, and his wife was standing on the porch holding a coffee mug, just staring. My cousin had to promise to rebuild it himself. He’s decent with masonry, but he’s been so busy trying to fix up his dirt bike that I doubt he’ll get around to it anytime soon. He bought the bike off Craigslist, and the guy swore it ran fine, but the carburetor was completely shot. 

So... wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right, the elevator. Yeah, it's definitely the trapped feeling. Like, what if the power goes out and nobody knows I'm in there? That's what really gets me.
